name: Chrome Don't Cry (It Conducts)
description:
Released in 2217 by augmentation-culture artist and DJ collective FRACTURE/BLOOM, 'Chrome Don't Cry (It Conducts)' is a six-minute neural-feed club track engineered for listeners with mid-grade to high-grade BCI augmentation. The track's surface layer — audible to anyone — is a dense, euphoric piece of polyrhythmic dance music built on Afrobeats-derived percussion architecture, Andean charango samples processed beyond recognition, and a bass register so physical it registers on building vibration sensors. But the neural feed layer, accessible only to those with compatible chrome, delivers a second simultaneous emotional experience: a slow, aching grief signal layered beneath the euphoria, a texture its producers describe as 'the feeling of missing something you can't name.' The contrast between the body's involuntary joy response and the neural grief layer is the entire point.

The song was written in the aftermath of the 2216 Augmentation Riot — three days of violence in the Circuit following the announcement that basic BCI upgrades would require Tier 3 financial certification, effectively locking Tier 1 and many Tier 2 residents out of standard augmentation access. FRACTURE/BLOOM said in a rare statement that the dual-layer design was intended to represent 'what it means to dance when you know the floor is being pulled out from under you.' The track became the anthem of the augmentation access movement and has been played at every major rally since.
creator: FRACTURE/BLOOM
genre: Neural Club, Afrobeats Fusion, Augmentation Culture, Dual-Layer Electronic
audience: Augmented individuals across Tier 1-3, augmentation access advocates, Circuit and the Gray Zone club culture, anyone who lost BCI upgrade access post-2216
cultural_impact: The track's dual-layer architecture has been analyzed extensively in academic and journalistic contexts as a technical and political statement — the first widely-distributed piece of music to deliberately weaponize the gap between augmented and unaugmented listening experience as social commentary. Corporate censors initially flagged it for 'unauthorized neural pathway stimulation design' before lawyers for the augmentation access movement successfully argued the grief-signal layer fell below restricted thresholds. It remains in gray-market distribution. The full neural version is the second most-copied data chip in the Gray Zone after 'Let the Ledger Rot.'
known_fans: augmented Circuit and the Gray Zone youth
BCI engineers sympathetic to access equity
story_hooks: A corporate neuroengineer discovers that the grief-signal layer of the track contains embedded data — not just emotional texture, but encoded information — and the question of what that information is and who it was meant to reach becomes urgent.

FRACTURE/BLOOM's identity has been kept secret, but a Vantablack Media subsidiary has traced one of the collective's members to a the Gray Zone address and is moving to make an arrest under the neural pathway regulation statute.

A character with no BCI augmentation attends a club where the track is playing and watches the augmented dancers around them experience something they cannot access — and has to decide how that makes them feel about the movement they've been supporting.
